people.role: Head of Phất Y Cốc since 1090, sword cultivation and swordsmen for hire; the valley's one Wind root
people.appearance: A tall, quiet man in an old grey robe with one long sleeve, who stands sideways to everyone as if he were about to leave.
people.backstory: Thạch Tàng Danh was a hawk-catcher's son on Thương Ưng Đài, the windy terrace of the Pivot's plateau, and the wind went into him there. He came to the valley at fifteen to sell a hawk and stayed for the sword. The second head Liễu Hành Vân (lieu_hanh_van) had kept the founder's grey sleeve and its Wind art closed for three centuries because no one could read it; he read it. He became head in 1090 and has hired out the valley's swords ever since, to the Pivot's war hall, the camel trains and the mines, by the founder's rule that a sword leaves when the deed is done. In 1130 the sword sage Tư Không Hạc Niên (tu_khong_hac_nien) came to the valley, and the two fought on Cùng Mục Phong for three days (C186). The chronicle calls it a draw. Thạch has never spoken of it (A232), and his disciples climb the peak to read the sword marks. He is three hundred, he has no Wind-rooted heir, and Cửu Cao Phái takes every Wind child born on the plateau before he hears of them.
people.wants: A Wind root to give the Brushed Sleeve Step to before he walks out of the valley as the founder did.
people.secret: He lost. On the third day Tư Không cut his left sleeve through and then lowered his sword, called it even and walked away without a sect, so that the valley would keep its head. The mended seam is under his arm.

people.appearance: A neat woman in a grey coat with ink on two fingers, who reads a client's hands before their letter.
people.backstory: Lam Khế Ngôn grew up among the camel drivers of Đà Đội Thôn, where her mother hired guards for the trains, and she came to the valley at sixteen with a better head for terms than for swords. Thạch Tàng Danh (thach_tang_danh) took her as his first disciple and in 1150 gave her the valley's Contract Seal. She has made Phất Y rich: the Pivot's war hall pays a standing fee for forty swords, the mines of Ngọc Hành hire their guards from her, and the camel trains will not cross the steppe without a grey sleeve. She has never been on a long hire herself. The head will not live another two hundred years, and she will be a Trúc Cơ for some time yet, which is the problem. She plays go with the Pivot's drillmaster Đái Hổ Thần (dai_ho_than) when he comes to sign the year's contract.
people.wants: To be head after Thạch, and to hire the valley's swords to anyone who pays, not only to the Pivot's friends.
people.secret: Since 1190 she has hired a company, under a camel-train name, to guard caravans of Thính Vũ Lâu's iron on the southern road.

people.role: Swordswoman back from twenty years on the caravan roads
people.appearance: Burnt dark by the road, with a scar that pulls one corner of her mouth into a smile she does not mean.
people.backstory: Born at the horse-drinking spring of Mã Ẩm Tuyền, where the ground is warm in winter, she went out on her first hire at thirty and came back at fifty. She guarded the trains of the merchant Kim Vạn Lý (kim_van_ly) across the western plains, and he still owes her a year's pay. Thạch Tàng Danh (thach_tang_danh) is her master. The swords of the valley would follow her before Lam Khế Ngôn (lam_khe_ngon), and both women know it.

people.role: Warden of Can Tương Khoáng, the ore the valley's swords are made of
people.appearance: A square, slow-spoken miner with a sword he uses mostly to point at ore.
people.backstory: He keeps the mine of Can Tương (A225) and sends its ore to Thối Tinh Môn's forge, where the valley's swords are made from it. He trusts the smiths and has noticed that Can Tương ore comes back as blades that ring more clearly than any star iron Hầu Thiết Anh (hau_thiet_anh) sells. He has not wondered why.

people.role: Founder of Phất Y Cốc (560); a Wind-rooted swordsman who brushed his sleeve and left after every deed
people.backstory: A wandering Wind-rooted swordsman who hired his sword for one deed at a time and left before he could be thanked. In 560 he settled the grassland valley under the Pivot, dug the ore of Can Tương for his students' swords (A225), and cut the verse of the hired sword into the cliff. In 790 he hung his grey robe in the hall, with his Wind art folded in the sleeve, and walked out. His disciple Liễu Hành Vân (lieu_hanh_van) kept the valley. He did not die then: on the ore road he took a ninety-year-old miner, Tư Không Hạc Niên (tu_khong_hac_nien), as his one disciple, gave him Cô Hạc, and was seen off from Tống Khách Thị in 900 (A138).

people.backstory: The founder Quách Vô Tích's (quach_vo_tich) disciple, who had no Wind and could not read his art. She kept it closed and built the valley a living instead: she made the Contract Seal, wrote the Dry Road Sword Primer for the camel-train companies, and sent the valley's swords to the Pivot under its writ in the War of Broken Halberds (C016). She gave the grey sleeve to Thạch Tàng Danh (thach_tang_danh) when he opened the book.
